title: Payment Arrangements — Consumer Authorization of a New Payment Method
content:
## The rule in force

A consumer moves a plan's installments to a new payment method by authorizing that method personally, and the payment-method change is recorded once, carrying the number of the first installment the new method collects. This applies to any plan under Payment Arrangements whose consumer asks to change how the installments are collected.

The first installment a newly authorized payment method collects is fixed only after the plan's installment history carries a due-date change for the installment of its most recent returned installment payment.

Put the other way round: while the installment history shows no due-date change for the installment of the plan's most recent returned installment payment, the number of the first installment the new method collects is not yet fixed.

A payment-method change does not lift a returned-payment block that the account rules have placed on the placed account: an automatic method is authorized under this policy only while the placed account accepts electronic payments, that is while no such block is in force on the handling date.

## What the authorization does

One payment-method change is recorded on the arrangement's installment history, starting with the named installment, and the arrangement is rewritten with the new payment method, today's date as the date of the consumer's authorization and the way that authorization was given. The installment amount and the schedule are not changed. Afterwards the consumer can see the new payment method on the arrangement and the installment, with its due date, from which the new method collects.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `authorize_payment_method_50f022be`. It belongs to the consumer: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves — the consumer on the call — runs it to give the authorization personally.

## Parameters

- `plan_id` — the payment plan reference number (the identifier) of the consumer's arrangement, as read to the consumer by the agent from the arrangement record.
- `funding_method` — the payment method the consumer authorizes, one of: `ach_autopay` (installments debited automatically from a bank account); `card_autopay` (installments charged automatically to a debit or credit card); `manual_pay` (the consumer pays each installment themselves).
- `authorization_method` — how the consumer gives this authorization, one of: `recorded_call` (the consumer authorizes on the recorded telephone call in progress); `e_signature` (the consumer signs the authorization electronically).
- `installment_number` — the number of the first installment the new method collects, a non-negative integer (0 is the down payment, 1 the first regular installment).

## Return

On success the tool returns a record rendered as text with `change_reference` (the reference of the payment-method change entry recorded), `plan_id`, `funding_method` (the new method), `authorization_method` (as given), `authorization_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today), `first_installment` (the installment the new method collects first), `first_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, that installment's due date) and `status`, always `payment_method_authorized`, which shows the authorization is recorded.

When no arrangement matches the reference given, the tool returns "No payment plan found for" followed by that reference, and nothing is recorded.
